name: Jet
description: A single-seat jet fighter on tricycle gear: one engine pushes from a nozzle behind its tail with more thrust than the jet weighs, so it climbs steeply, and it flies level on its own near cruising speed.
comment: A vehicle preset (#728): see sedan.json for the format and plane.json for a plane's (chassis.aircraft, the inert engine and transmission, the landing gear, the camera and the derive block are as there). A jet fighter: chassis.aircraft has no propeller block, so its engine is a jet, pushing from a nozzle at engines.x, 50 cm behind the fuselage's rear end at -950, at the fuselage's middle height (200, 5 cm below the centre of mass); the grey body draws the nozzle as a short box on the nozzle bone and an intake each side of the fuselage, and nothing spins. 9000 kg on one engine of 100 kN, more than its 88.2 kN weight, so it climbs steeply; a 28 m^2 wing of 980 cm span on a deep 300 cm chord, with a jet's thin 2 degrees of camber and 2.6 degrees of aileron (12 rolled it at 415 degrees a second, over a turn a second, with D held all the way; the roll is in proportion to the aileron's angle, 212 degrees a second at 6, so 2.6 gives about 90 at the 120 m/s cruise speed, a full roll in 4 seconds, as measured in flight; the aileron does not enter the trim); a 6 m^2 tailplane and a 300 cm fin of 5 m^2, twice the plane's and taller; a 1500 cm fuselage on tricycle gear 520 cm long, the mains 60 cm behind the centre of mass (12 percent of the weight on the nose wheel); a 250 m/s limit. The trim is plane.json's arithmetic (MantleChassisDefinitions.cpp) on the jet's thrust line, with one term the first version of it lacked: the fuselage's drag is applied by the chassis module at its own position, the root body's origin on the ground, not at the centre of mass (FChassisSimModule::Simulate, AddLocalForce), so its 4.8 kN, 2.05 m below the centre of mass, pitches the nose down by 9.8 kN m (PLANE_BODY_DRAG_POINT in validate.py). Flight tests found it: held level at 120 m/s by its autopilot the jet needed 0.18 degrees of elevator nose-up of the arithmetic's, and let go with -0.7 degrees of camber it sank 91 m in 20 s as it settled at 124 m/s, not 120; the arithmetic with the term wants 0.21 degrees, a pitch of 0.39 against the 0.5 held and a throttle of 0.2553 against the 0.255 held. At cruiseSpeed, 120 m/s (q = 8820 Pa, the weight 88.2 kN), the wing flies at 0.39 degrees of pitch with a lift coefficient of 0.37 = 2 sin((0.39 + 2) x 4.5 degrees), 92.3 kN; the tail, 6.35 m aft, pushes down 4.3 kN, a lift coefficient of -0.08 = 2 sin((0.39 - 0.9 + control) x 4.5 degrees), a control angle of -0.01 degrees: -0.9 degrees of camber centres the elevator at 120 m/s. schema/validate.py holds cruiseThrottle 0.255 within 0.02 of the 0.2553 level flight there needs, and the elevator within 0.05 of centre at 120 m/s (-0.001), within 0.16 from 108 to 132 m/s (-0.035 and +0.024) and within the stick's 0.5 from 102 to 156 m/s (-0.057 and +0.058): 0.85 to 1.3 of cruise, as the plane's 59.5 to 91 m/s are of its 70. Measured in the probe with these numbers: let go at 120 m/s with the throttle at cruise and the stick centred, it holds 120.0 to 120.4 m/s and its height to within 8 m over 20 s (and 9 m over 40 s), against the plane's 14 m. The take-off, the same forces on the gear (validate.py): from rest the throttle lever reaches full in 2 s, and 100 kN less the drag (5.5 kN at lift-off) pushes the 9000 kg at up to 11 m/s^2; the stick held back lifts the nose wheel from 37.4 m/s, and turned 8 degrees nose-up the wing (a lift coefficient of 1.41 = 2 sin((8 + 2) x 4.5 degrees)) and the thrust's upward 13.9 kN hold the weight at 57.5 m/s, after 155 m and 6.3 s: well inside the 800 m runway, where the plane rolls 313 m. Level at 250 m/s it needs 94 percent throttle, so the limit, not its drag, sets its top speed. Its ranges are a jet's: up to 16 t, springs up to 5000 and brakes up to 15000.
